analysis.title: TMT Today 11.4.26 - 4 Nov 2026
key_insights: Index futures moved off overnight highs (Nasdaq +40bps, S&P +90bps, Russell +140bps) as markets absorbed the midterm results, in which Democrats won the House and the Senate.
GS Econ expects Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to seek limits on the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs and reverse spending cuts enacted last year.

GS Econ says the election is less likely to change federal data center and AI regulation, which needs bipartisan Senate support and must overcome a veto. State and local Democratic wins are likely to bring short-term data center moratoria that could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.
Election movers in TMT: hyperscalers higher versus neoclouds lower, SPCX and TSLA lower, power stocks lower.

AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.4bn against GS $13.3bn and Street $13.1bn. Datacenter revenue grew 97% y/y to $8.5bn. Q4 revenue guidance midpoint of $17.0bn is above the Street at $16.3bn and below GS at $17.6bn.

AMD expects CY27 Datacenter revenue growth of well over 100% y/y and total revenue growth of over 80%. Initial MI455 shipments went to customers in Q3 and OEMs including HPE, Dell, Lenovo and SuperMicro are expected to ramp in Q4.

ANET beat on EPS, revenue and margin and raised 2026 guidance to revenue growth of about 48% y/y at the midpoint. Initial 2027 outlook is revenue growth of 38-40% y/y, gross margin of 62-64%, EBIT margin of 49%, AI revenue doubling to $7bn and campus revenue of $2bn. GS raised its above-consensus 2027/28 EPS by about 10% to $6.13/$7.83.
GS flags ANET pushback areas as the q/q decline in deferred revenue and the deceleration in bookings growth.

DDOG Q3 revenue was $1.2bn (+35% y/y) in line with elevated expectations. Q4 revenue guidance of $1.19-1.2bn (+25% y/y) is against consensus of $1.2bn, with a guided operating margin of 23%. The stock fell 19% pre-market, with MDB, SNOW and NET lower in sympathy.
UBER Q3 gross bookings of $59.82bn were slightly below GSe $60.06bn and in line with Street $59.83bn. Q4 bookings guidance of $63.25-65.25bn compares with GSe $65.08bn and Street $64.26bn.

BKNG was mixed. Q3 gross bookings, room nights and adjusted EBITDA beat, revenue missed on product mix and booking timing, and Q4 room nights were guided below. Management flagged Middle East conflict and European unrest as headwinds through year end.

DUOL beat on bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA, raised FY26 guidance on all three metrics, and DAUs grew 29% y/y, accelerating from 23% in Q2. Q4 guidance implies modest gross margin pressure and roughly flat adjusted EBITDA y/y.

SMCI reported F1Q27 EPS of $1.81 on revenue of $19.9bn and gross margin of 12.8%. It raised FY27 revenue guidance to $72-82bn from $65-72bn, constrained by component availability and customer data center readiness.
SMCI management does not expect to need additional capital for the raised FY27 outlook and cited working capital improvement.
GS reinstated Skyworks at Sell with a 12-month target of $78. The Qorvo combination brings diversification and synergies, but about 60% smartphone exposure is expected to dampen growth.
Macro: Asia was mixed overnight (Japan down nearly 1.5%, Hong Kong up over 1.5%, China up over 2%), Europe up over 1%, back-end Treasury yields down about 4bp and WTI down 0.9%.
Calendar: Wednesday US Services PMI and EU flash inflation, Thursday BoE rates decision, Friday US nonfarm payrolls (prior +29k).

earnings_insights: AMD Q3 reported: revenue $13.4bn (GS $13.3bn, Street $13.1bn), non-GAAP operating EPS $2.09 (GS $2.03, Street $1.95), gross margin 55.9% (GS 56.2%, Street 56.1%), operating margin 29% (GS 28.7%, Street 28.0%), Datacenter revenue $8.5bn (GS $8.26bn, Street $8.24bn).

AMD Q4 guidance: revenue midpoint $17.0bn (GS est $17.6bn, Street est $16.3bn), non-GAAP gross margin 55% (GS est 54.4%, Street est 55.3%), implied non-GAAP EPS ex SBC $2.92 (GS est $2.97, Street est $2.65).

ANET Q3 2026 reported: beat on EPS, revenue and margin. Raised 2026 guidance to revenue growth of about 48% y/y at the midpoint. Initial 2027 outlook: revenue growth 38-40%, gross margin 62-64%, EBIT margin 49%. GS 2027/28 EPS estimates $6.13/$7.83.

DDOG Q3 reported: revenue $1.2bn (+35% y/y) against guidance of $1.135-1.145bn, operating margin 28%. Q4 guidance: revenue $1.19-1.2bn (+25% y/y) against consensus est $1.2bn, operating margin guided to 23%.

UBER Q3 reported: gross bookings $59.82bn (GSe $60.06bn, Street est $59.83bn), revenue $14.77bn (GSe $14.58bn, Street est $14.67bn), adjusted EBITDA $2.96bn (GSe $2.90bn, Street est $2.92bn), non-GAAP EPS $0.88 (GSe and Street est $0.86). Q4 guidance: bookings $63.25-65.25bn (GSe $65.08bn, Street est $64.26bn), non-GAAP EPS $0.95-0.99 (GSe $0.98, Street est $0.97).

BKNG Q3 reported: gross bookings, room nights and adjusted EBITDA above GSe, Street and company guidance, revenue below estimates. Q4 room nights guided below. Marketing expense +11% y/y. Management is on track for $650m of annual run-rate savings in 2027.
DUOL Q3 reported: bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA above GSe, Street and guidance. DAUs +29% y/y. FY26 guidance raised on all three metrics. Q4 adjusted EBITDA guided roughly flat y/y.

SMCI F1Q27 reported: EPS $1.81 (guidance $1.01-1.10), revenue $19.9bn (preannounced $18.5-19.5bn, original guidance $14.5-15.5bn), gross margin 12.8% (preannounced 12.0-12.5%, original guidance 10.4-10.8%). FY27 revenue guidance raised to $72-82bn from $65-72bn.
Pre-market reactions as listed: AMD +1.5% (after +10% on the initial reaction), DDOG -19%, ANET +6.5% (up as much as +18% overnight), SMCI +5%, UBER +1.5%, BKNG +1%, DUOL +16%.

Earnings still to come Wednesday after the close include QCOM, APP, ARM, SNAP, MELI, HUBS, COHR and EXPE. Wednesday pre-market included DDOG, UBER, CRCL, CDW and NYT. Thursday after the close includes ABNB, NET, AXON, MCHP, LYFT, DKNG and TEAM.

tension_points.bull_case: Federal AI and data center regulation is less likely to change since it needs bipartisan Senate support and must overcome a veto.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic wins at the state and local level are likely to lead to short-term data center moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.

tension_points.bull_case: The Qorvo combination brings revenue diversification, manufacturing and SG&A cost synergies and potentially improved RF industry profitability.
tension_points.bear_case: About 60% exposure to smartphones is expected to dampen growth in the medium term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of abating smartphone market headwinds or a broader re-rating in peer valuations would make GS more constructive.
